video_title: Major Drama Coming From The Jazz At The Draft?

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Utah Jazz face uncertainty with the second overall draft pick
quotes.excerpt: I don't believe they know which guy they're picking.
quotes.quote: There are three alternatives and I don't believe that the Jazz know who's going to be there. Number one, they don't know who's going to be there. Number two, whoever is there at two, I don't believe they know which guy they're picking. If it's AJ Dybantsa, if it's Darren Peterson, if it's Cameron Boozer, I think all those three guys are in play for the Jazz at this point.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jazz lack a clear-cut face of the franchise player
quotes.excerpt: They still don't have a clear-cut face of the franchise.
quotes.quote: The Jazz have done a lot of things over the last year to build up their roster to put themselves in a chance to be competitive this year, to compete for a postseason spot. They still don't have a clear-cut face of the franchise. Jaren Jackson Jr. is a very good player, not a face of a franchise. Same with Lauri Markkanen. Keyonte George took a major leap last year, not a face of the franchise. Walker Kessler has the potential to maybe be that guy, but no sure thing. They've got to pick a guy at two who has a chance to develop into that sort of a player.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating Jaren Jackson Jr. and Cameron Boozer as a duo
quotes.excerpt: You could see them as a great complementary duo.
quotes.quote: Jaren Jackson Jr.'s flaw playing the five is he's a poor rebounder for a five. Well, Boozer would really mitigate that concern because he's a really strong rebounder for a four. Boozer as a four, part of the concern is you really need a rim protector alongside him. Obviously, Jaren Jackson Jr. is an elite rim protector, so those guys you could see them as a great complementary duo. I'm not saying that's how they would start, but just playing significant minutes together.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Contract extension negotiations for Jaren Jackson Jr. and Keyonte George
quotes.excerpt: I'm not sure the agency feels as strongly about their fit.
quotes.quote: He's represented by the same agency that represents Keyonte George. My understanding is the Jazz think those two guys could fit very well. Keyonte is kind of a 1.5, Peterson is kind of a 1.5. Peterson is probably more of a two than a one. Keyonte had a breakout year last year. I'm not sure the agency feels as strongly about their fit, but I think the agency's opinion might be influenced by the unlikelihood of Keyonte George getting a contract extension this summer.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jazz financial outlook and contract negotiations
quotes.excerpt: The trade for Jaren Jackson Jr. really vaulted them from a payroll perspective.
quotes.quote: The Jazz, they want to be good. That means they're going to have to negotiate hard. They're obviously not going to be a free agency destination. They're becoming very expensive. The trade for Jaren Jackson Jr. really vaulted them from a payroll perspective. Lauri is obviously on a max. Just like they've been negotiating hard with Walker Kessler, which I promise we're getting to soon, I think they're going to take the same approach with Keyonte George.
